<subject>Re: GreenEarth Commodities</subject>
<body>
I think our discussion about an incremental charge applying to customers of all statuses was with regard to our speculation on how the "new MCP" payback mechanism would work, not Nashik.  I think the payback mechanism is still speculation. There are many differing alternatives.

That's my recollection.


From: Thomas Gade on 28-05-2024 11:05 AM
To: Reyansh Krish
cc: Chakradhar Lala, Hardik D Pal, Nihal Karan, Ekantika Nagarajan 
Subject: RE: GreenEarth Commodities

I've talked to Chakradhar.  I think I just misunderstood.

	Thomas Gade 23-05-2024 09:26 AM 	   To: Chakradhar 
Lala  cc: Nihal Karan, Ekantika 
Nagarajan, Reyansh Krish, Hardik D 
Pal  Subject: RE: GreenEarth Commodities


Chakradhar, Nihal Karan, Reyansh Krish and I were on a trip with Viraj Vyas last week.  I understood from Nihal that Viraj may believe that all customers, including direct access, should pay the increase you mention.  Nihal?  This was encouraging from a litigation exposure standpoint because, to the extent all consumers are treated alike, our DA customers who were resourced to utility service cannot claim to have been disadvantaged by our action.  The converse is also true:  if they have to pay because they were put back on utility service they may try to pass that cost through to us.  To the extent that any increase is to pay back Kisan Agro for buying wheat 1/2/24-3/30/25, and those on DA are not required to pay this, AgriProcure could have a substantial exposure to its customers.   Maybe we need to modify our strategy to take this into account. -----Original Message-----
From:  Lala, Chakradhar  
Sent: Thursday, 23-05-2024 8:48 AM
To: Karan, Nihal; Bala, Peter; Sura, Qabil; Gade, Thomas; 
Mumbai, Ahmedabad; Stoness, AgroCorp; Bakhshi, Tamara
Cc: Brahmbhatt, Vedhika; Pal, Hardik; Hora, Ronith; Mangat, Vrinda; Krish, Reyansh
Subject: GreenEarth Commodities


Maharashtra State Co-op's filing confirms that the MSP rate freeze of ₹25/kg does not apply to direct access.

In hearings on Maharashtra State Co-op's potential rate increase for large customers:
Maharashtra State Co-op has proposed to allocate all retained wheat to small customers (below 100 tonnes).  Large customers would be served  by Kisan Agro (or be direct access).  It's apparent several parties have major problems with this. It is interesting that Maharashtra State Co-op has calculated the expected rate increase under their plan as ₹1.50/kg.  If large customers are allocated a piece of retained wheat, the increase goes up to ₹1.65/kg.  In the latter case, large customers retain a CTC (related to contract farming and other long term stranded costs) that they would lose in the former case. Our involvement is to get an order 1) excluding DA from any rate increase (the proposed ₹1.50/kg) 2) excluding DA from any surcharge related to undercollection from the rate freeze (an amount that is not known at this point) 3) prorating the surcharge related to undercollection if the customer
